cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Experience performing or coordinating financial transactions such as purchasing, travel and entertainment reimbursement, invoice processing, reconciliation, and record keeping.
Substantial experience supporting a dean, vice chancellor, chair, or other senior executive in a complex higher-education or similarly decentralized organization.
Experience independently coordinating high-profile meetings, events, reviews, or executive projects involving multiple senior stakeholders.

Under the direction of the Senior Assistant Dean, the Executive Assistant provides professional, confidential, and high-level administrative support to the Dean of Baskin Engineering and helps ensure the effective operation of the Dean's Office. The incumbent independently oversees the Dean's complex calendar and executive workflow, coordinates leadership meetings, events, communications, and follow-up, oversees office operations and financial transactions, and provides administrative and project support to the Assistant and Associate Deans. The Executive Assistant serves as a trusted liaison with faculty, staff, students, campus leaders, external partners, and other executive offices, and independently researches, analyzes, and resolves complex administrative issues. The incumbent exercises a high degree of judgment, initiative, political acumen, confidentiality, and discretion in setting priorities, anticipating needs, developing solutions, and managing multiple high-priority demands in a fast-paced academic environment.
Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment in handling highly confidential or sensitive personnel, academic, financial, and institutional information.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work primarily on campus, with periods of remote work possible based on operational needs. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.

Exercise the utmost discretion in managing sensitive information learned in the course of performing their duties. Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information, and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment. Understands that sensitive information should be shared on a limited basis and actively takes steps to limit access to sensitive information to individuals who have legitimate business need to know. Ensure that sensitive information is properly safeguarded. Follow all organizational policies and laws on data protection and privacy. This includes secure handling of physical and digital records and proper usage of IT systems to prevent data leaks. The unauthorized or improper disclosure of confidential work-related information obtained from any source on any work-related matter is a violation of these expectations.
Advanced organizational and time-management skills, with demonstrated ability to independently manage a complex executive calendar, competing priorities, and rapidly changing demands.
Thorough knowledge of UC Santa Cruz or comparable higher-education administrative structures, policies, protocols, and procedures.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.
Demonstrated reliability, responsiveness, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through on sensitive and time-critical work.
Knowledge of applicable records-management, privacy, accessibility, and student-information requirements, including FERPA where relevant.
Ability to ascend/descend ladders with or without accommodation.
Exceptional attention to detail, accuracy, and quality, including the ability to independently review and correct work before completion.
Ability to safely perform the physical requirements necessary to move light to moderate objects up to 60 lbs., with or without accommodation.
Advanced ability to organize and coordinate executive-office operations, establish priorities, anticipate needs, and develop effective administrative systems and procedures.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to research and synthesize information, evaluate alternatives, and resolve complex or unprecedented administrative issues with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to occasionally work overtime with little or no advance notice.
Excellent written communication skills with the ability to draft, edit, and proofread executive-level correspondence, reports, briefings, and presentations.
Ability to respond to emergencies after hours as necessary.
Excellent verbal communication skills, including active listening and diplomacy.
Ability to work overtime including evenings, nights, weekends and holidays to meet operational needs, and work an alternate work schedule shift as required.
Strong interpersonal skills and political acumen to navigate sensitive situations and communicate effectively with senior leaders and diverse internal and external constituencies.
Ability to travel to multiple work locations on and off campus.
Demonstrated project management skills, including developing work plans, coordinating multiple contributors, tracking deliverables, and completing complex assignments within demanding timeframes.
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.

Advanced proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office Suite, and the ability to learn and use organization-specific administrative, financial, and collaboration systems, including Slack for internal communications and Asana for task management.
Demonstrated commitment to professional, respectful, responsive, and inclusive service with the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
